title: How to Choose Full-Stack Observability for NVIDIA AI Factories | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA publishes a decision framework for monitoring GPU clusters that implicitly concedes a costly failure mode: 'gray failures' such as a single InfiniBand link drifting into elevated bit error rate can silently burn hours of a multi-day distributed training job while dashboards stay green. The prescribed minimum stack for a DGX/InfiniBand cluster is IPMI + DCGM + NVSM + UFM + BCM unified in Prometheus/Grafana, with NetQ, NMX, Run:ai and NIM added only when Ethernet, rack-scale NVLink, scheduling fairness or inference SLOs enter scope.

themes.theme: Gray failure economics in AI factories

insights.claim: A single InfiniBand link drifting into an elevated bit error rate can degrade a three-day distributed training job for six hours before the cause is traced, while GPU utilization and queue wait times still read normal.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: Effective GPU-hour yield in large clusters is materially below nameplate utilization; monitoring vendors and fabric-diagnostic tooling capture value from that gap.
insights.quote: Consider a distributed training job that is three days into execution. GPU utilization and queue wait times remain normal. After six hours of reduced throughput, the team traces the cause to a single InfiniBand link drifting into an elevated bit error rate.
insights.locator: Consider a distributed training job that

insights.claim: Because AI training follows the bulk synchronous parallel model, one slow rank stalling during NCCL all-reduce drags cluster-wide throughput down to the slowest rank and blocks every other rank — degradation, not outage, is the dominant loss mechanism.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: Cluster economics are governed by tail behavior, so scale-out buyers should underwrite fabric quality and straggler detection, not just peak FLOPS.
insights.quote: AI training follows the bulk synchronous parallel (BSP) model. These tightly coupled systems are sensitive to stragglers: one slow rank holds back the job.
insights.locator: This is a classic gray failure

insights.claim: The binding constraint in AI factory operations is not missing telemetry but signal selection — the required data already exists in deployed tools and the failure is in choosing which signals to act on early enough.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: Value in the AI-ops layer accrues to correlation/triage products, not to yet another metric collector or exporter.
insights.quote: The required telemetry typically already exists; the challenge is selecting the right signals from the right tools early enough to act.
insights.locator: You see this failure mode often in AI factories

themes.theme: NVIDIA's telemetry tool map and overlaps

insights.claim: NVIDIA now fields at least eight overlapping first-party telemetry products — DCGM, NVSM, UFM, NetQ, NMX, BCM, Run:ai, and NIM — plus Redfish/IPMI, and needs a published decision matrix to tell customers which ones they can skip.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: Portfolio sprawl in NVIDIA's software stack is a lock-in asset but also an integration tax that leaves room for third-party observability vendors.
insights.locator: Map AI infrastructure components to telemetry tools

insights.claim: DCGM and NVSM overlap on GPU metrics but neither substitutes for platform BMC data, so operators of DGX-class nodes are told to run DCGM for Prometheus export and retain NVSM for drive/power/system health.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: Even NVIDIA's own stack cannot be consolidated to one agent, confirming multi-tool spend per node is structural rather than transitional.
insights.quote: The tools overlap on GPU metrics; neither substitutes for platform BMC data.
insights.locator: DCGM compared to NVSM for GPUs

insights.claim: Fabric monitoring splits strictly by transport — UFM for InfiniBand and NetQ for Spectrum Ethernet/RoCE — with both deployed only in mixed-fabric estates, making the tool choice a direct readout of a customer's networking vendor decision.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: UFM versus NetQ attach rates are a proxy for the InfiniBand-vs-Ethernet share shift inside AI data centers.
insights.quote: Select by fabric type. InfiniBand uses UFM. Spectrum Ethernet/RoCE uses NetQ. Deploy both only when both fabrics are present.

insights.claim: NMX is positioned as required only for rack-scale NVLink and explicitly omittable on classic multi-node NVLink topologies where DCGM already covers node interconnects.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: NMX adoption tracks the installed base of rack-scale NVLink systems, making it a leading indicator of NVL72-class deployment penetration.
insights.quote: Required for rack-scale NVLink. Omit on classic multi-node NVLink topologies where DCGM already covers node interconnects.

insights.claim: BCM is framed as an aggregator and cluster/job control plane rather than a source of low-level counters, so it cannot displace the specialized telemetry tools beneath it.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: The aggregation layer is where NVIDIA extends control upward into cluster management, competing with Slurm/Kubernetes-native ops stacks.
insights.quote: Treat BCM as the aggregator and cluster/job plane, not as the source of low-level counters.

insights.claim: Run:ai and NIM are gated behind explicit business triggers — workload scheduling fairness and inference SLOs becoming first-class operational requirements — and neither replaces GPU or fabric monitoring.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: Run:ai and NIM revenue expands only as customers move from training-dominant to inference-in-production estates — a maturity marker to watch.
insights.quote: Introduce when workload scheduling fairness or inference SLOs are first-class operational requirements. Neither replaces DCGM or fabric monitoring.

themes.theme: Alert design and the watermelon-metrics problem

insights.claim: Adding exporters without a triage path produces 'watermelon metrics' — dashboards green on the outside while services fail inside — and the recommended corrective is deleting unused signals rather than accumulating them.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: Reusable mental model for judging any AI-ops vendor: coverage claims mean nothing without a mapped remediation action.
insights.quote: The result is “watermelon metrics”: dashboards that look green outside while services fail inside.
insights.locator: Teams keep adding metrics and dashboards

insights.claim: The prescribed InfiniBand top-k alert set names specific counters — Effective_BER, Total_Raw_BER, SymbolErrorCounterExtended, PortXmitDataExtended, Chip_Temp on the fabric side and DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS, GPU_UTIL, MEM_COPY_UTIL, POWER_USAGE on the GPU side — each of which must map to an action such as drain node, replace cable, or open a fabric case.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: Cable and optics replacement is an ongoing consumable cost line in AI clusters, not a one-time build expense.
insights.quote: InfiniBand: PortXmitDataExtended, SymbolErrorCounterExtended, Effective_BER, Total_Raw_BER, Chip_Temp.
insights.locator: Build an actionable AI infrastructure alert set

insights.claim: NVIDIA steers operators toward Prometheus/Grafana as the single scrape and visualization plane, noting DCGM and NVSM expose Prometheus endpoints and UFM/BCM feed the same model, explicitly to avoid a second control plane before gNMI or SNMP is required.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: The open Prometheus/Grafana pairing is the de facto AI-factory telemetry substrate, favoring vendors that plug into it over proprietary agents.
insights.quote: Prefer Prometheus exporters where available: DCGM and NVSM both expose Prometheus endpoints; UFM and BCM can feed the same scrape model via exporters or APIs.

insights.claim: The recommended operating model is two-layer: a Grafana board answers 'GPU, node, or fabric?' first, and vendor UIs such as the UFM web UI or BCM Base View are only opened once the failing domain is identified.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: Day-2 operations cost, not procurement, is emerging as the differentiator between AI cloud operators at similar hardware scale.
insights.quote: Layer 1 is the Grafana dashboard used first: is the fault in the GPU, node, or fabric? Layer 2 is the vendor UI deep dive (UFM web UI, BCM Base View, and similar tools) once the failing domain is known.

insights.claim: Observability maturity should be scored by time-to-name-the-failing-component-and-next-action relative to compute wasted, not by dashboard count — a metric the author repeats verbatim at both the middle and end of the post.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: A concrete diligence question for anyone underwriting a GPU cloud: how many GPU-hours are lost per incident before the failing component is named.
insights.quote: Measure it by whether your signals show the failing component and the next action before significant compute capacity is wasted.
insights.locator: Don’t measure observability maturity by the number of dashboards

insights.claim: NVIDIA states DGX and HGX deployments share the same observability surface despite differing hardware configurations, meaning the tooling and operational playbook transfer across NVIDIA's own systems and OEM-built HGX boxes.
insights.speaker: Jorge Cardoso
insights.so_what: Software-layer lock-in extends to OEM HGX systems, so NVIDIA captures operational stickiness even where it does not sell the server.
insights.quote: NVIDIA DGX and NVIDIA HGX deployments share the same observability surface, even when hardware configurations differ
